notes: Additional rotated whole-workload-pass runner; all 962 official and 714 supplemental queries, four commands, seven samples after ten-second warmup per engine/command, same CPU 2 for driver and engines. It complements the archived upstream runner rather than silently replacing it.

Original, V4, selected, shared-reader, direct-window and selected-Simd4x controls are unchanged verified binaries; the refined block-intersection candidate changes only scoring.rs and two crate-private current-block slice views in posting.rs. No format, scoring-model or query-list change.

Fresh candidate gates cover rounded and group indexes: exact COUNT against Tantivy, pruned top-10/100/1000 against exhaustive scoring, and complete ordered top-1000 IDs/score bits/counts equal verified V4 across all 1676 queries.

The native block prototype passes 29 scoring tests, focused integration suites, Clippy and both complete ARM cross-source oracles. No new WASM build was run for these native iterations, following the user instruction.

Local first-block runs are separate from the refined and clean repeats. The first refined ARM run overlapped an accidental recursive source search and is excluded from performance conclusions; refined-run-contamination.json records it. Only block-conjunction-clean-arm timing is the final refined ARM comparison.

All encoded indexes match per-file manifests before and after timing. Simd4x uses matched document order and the same selected binary. Profiling, hashing, compilation and transfers are outside latency measurement.

Disassembly records static code and source identity; normalized counts are not executed instruction or cycle measurements. Initial Apple objdump symbol filtering failed; the retained local analysis uses validated nonempty address ranges.

Exact byte duplicates are stored once with file-aliases.json and restore_aliases.py. Every original logical path retains its own size and hash; no query, score bit or timing sample is omitted. Binaries and raw perf data remain in the separately hashed full archive.
Warm single-query measurements do not establish cold-cache, concurrent-ingest, sparse-index or overall search-engine superiority.
